main_topics: TSH creeping up on stable levothyroxine dose
calcium supplement timing and drug interaction
output.reason_for_conversation: understanding why thyroid control has drifted
output.summary: User reported a steady three-check climb in TSH (1.5 to 3.6) despite unchanged levothyroxine dose over a year, and asked what could cause this. The bot identified calcium supplement timing as a likely culprit—started a year ago and taken at breakfast, too close to the morning levothyroxine dose—and explained other factors including progressive thyroid gland loss in Hashimoto's disease. The user expressed reassurance about the mechanism and accepted a concrete plan: separate the calcium by several hours, mention the trend and mild fatigue to their doctor, and recheck TSH in six to eight weeks.
